analysis.title: From Tech To Bonds The Next Big Positioning Shock Is Taking Shape
key_insights: Deutsche Bank is tactically cautious on tech. Mega-cap growth and tech have about 4 percentage points of relative upside to the top of their long-term trend channel versus potentially 16 points of downside if past rotation patterns repeat.
This is the fifth major rotation into tech in two years, and prior reversals were sharp, inverted V-shaped moves.
DB expects mega-cap growth and tech earnings up about 55% y/y in Q3, but argues this may not sustain outperformance because investors are questioning future profitability.
DB expects about 21% earnings growth outside tech, which it says the market underappreciates.

The S&P 500 equal-weight index relative to Nasdaq 100 is bouncing off the lower end of its long-term trend channel. Positioning remains tilted to mega-cap growth and tech, and the rest of the market is relatively underowned.
DRAM ETF broke below its short-term trend line and its 50-day moving average, and was down another 5% premarket to 51.8. It is set for its most oversold reading since inception at the open.
Goldman's Memory basket fell 9.3% between October 5 and 12 and AI Semiconductors fell 6.7%. Nasdaq underperformed the S&P 500 by 1.7 percentage points over the same period.

The Nasdaq futures premium versus S&P futures has started reversing. CFTC data showed gross Nasdaq futures longs in the Other trader category at one-year highs as of October 6, a potentially vulnerable pocket of positioning.
KOSPI broke below its 200-day moving average and closed further below it than at any point since before the 2025 melt-up began. The triangle-like formation delivered its downside break.
KOSPI VIX has spiked as the index fell, a shift from the spot-up, vol-up behavior seen during the melt-up. It points to panic in Korean volatility.
NDX implied volatility remains relatively subdued despite memory weakness and heavy tech overweights, so Nasdaq downside hedges look relatively cheap.
Goldman highlights significant upside convexity in bond prices for CTAs. Shorts remain substantial, so a modest reversal could trigger aggressive covering.

Morgan Stanley: France's 2027 budget assumes 10-year yields averaging 4.3%, while OAT yields were around 4.9%. A sustained 100bp rise in borrowing costs adds €3.4bn to annual interest expense initially, rising to €33bn after ten years.

Goldman's Rikin Shah: France bears the higher global cost of capital from the AI investment boom without the growth benefits, which are concentrated in the US. Marginal French borrowing cost is about 250bp above the effective rate on existing debt.
